numericalAssumptions: Earth gravitational parameter 398600.4418 km³/s² and spherical surface radius 6371 km.
Fixed inertial 2D plane; point-mass two-body gravity.
Universal-variable Kepler propagation with Stumpff functions, bracketed bisection, and elliptic period reduction.
Instantaneous impulses specified in m/s; along-track is perpendicular to radius in the angular-motion direction, not the instantaneous eccentric-orbit velocity direction.
Surface-event detection uses at most 10-second intervals and checks any intervening perigee; contact time is bisected.
Hohmann guidance assumes the current radius belongs to a circular initial orbit; warns for eccentric current trajectories.
limitations: No atmosphere, J2, Earth rotation, third bodies, thrust duration, fuel accounting, relativistic effects, or live data.
Geostationary-radius scenario does not model ground tracks.
At 2 million km spacecraft distance the run pauses; the threshold may be overshot by one animation-frame advance.
Conic paths use 440 plot segments and are clipped inside Earth and beyond 5 million km; plot geometry is for visualization.
Near-radial degenerate trajectories have no plotted conic when angular momentum approaches zero.
Maximum requested speed is 3600×; the per-frame real-time increment is capped at 0.1 s, so background or slow frames do not catch up wall-clock time.
Only the latest 20 burn records are shown, while cumulative applied delta-v includes all burns.
No persisted state or network services.
